title: Khosla family’s purchase of Seattle Seahawks approved by NFL owners
content:
ATLANTA — On Wednesday, NFL owners voted unanimously to approve the sale of the Seattle Seahawks to Vinod and Neeru Khosla.

The vote was part of a special league meeting held almost exclusively for that purpose.

On July 11, the Seahawks announced the Paul G. Allen estate had reached an agreement with the Khoslas to sell the franchise for an NFL record $9.612 billion. Allen’s sister, Jody, had operated the team since he died in 2018.

“The task ahead is actually pretty simple,” Vinod Khosla said Wednesday, shortly after the vote. “Keep the winning streak alive. Get another Super Bowl. That’s simple. In general, our approach is generally going to be long-term focused. That’s our inclination always. So keep winning, take a long-term approach, and learn a lot.”

The Seahawks are the third NFL team to sell in the past decade, following the Carolina Panthers’ $2.275 billion sale to David Tepper in 2018 and the Washington Commanders going to Josh Harris for approximately $6 billion two years ago.

Vinod and Neeru Khosla were born in India and immigrated to the U.S. to continue their education and eventually launch careers as entrepreneurs. Vinod is considered one of Silicon Valley’s most influential innovators and investors. He was an early investor in Google and has made several investments in AI. Neeru Khosla, who met Vinod in India when the two were children, earned two master’s degrees, including one in molecular biology. Neeru will be the controlling owner of the Seahawks; their son, Neal, is expected to have a major role in the team.

The Khoslas join the Minnesota Vikings’ Zygi Wilf (Germany) and the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Shahid Khan (Pakistan) as the only other principal owners born outside the U.S.

Though the Khoslas have been understood as the Seahawks’ next owners for more than a month, the belief around the league is that no major changes within the organization will take place imminently.

“This has been them getting in the building,” one league source, speaking on condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to discuss an ownership situation publicly, told The Athletic last week. “They’re not doing anything until they get in the building.”

The franchise comes with stability in the football operations department. General manager John Schneider signed an extension two years ago that has him locked in through 2031. Mike Macdonald, the third-youngest head coach to ever win a Super Bowl, signed a six-year deal in 2024.

“It’s not very often you can buy a Super Bowl championship team, but you’ve done that,” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a press conference. “Many of our owners struggle to find ways to get into the Super Bowl and win a trophy, and you’ll be walking into your new building shortly with a fresh, shiny trophy there for you.”
